text.tspan: Hands cultivate a garden with care.
When we reduce everyday waste, a little care can make the experience better. Planning and
thinking about other people both help.
First, changing one repeat purchase can reduce waste over time. For example, we bring a
reusable bag and refill a bottle. This is a small thing that makes the day easier.
Second, local knowledge makes shared action more effective. For example, we check the local
recycling rules before sorting materials. We do not need a perfect day to do this well.
We can reduce everyday waste more easily when we prepare and notice other people. These
simple steps give us a useful place to start.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the
conclusion. Each body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the
argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Ask a friend to help you reduce everyday waste. Explain two things you can do together. Use four short paragraphs:
introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: say what you want to do; explain the first
step; explain a different second step; say why the two steps help.)
